<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `49401bfa148e3f2426fa9b9768f73a896dce309c` — the merge of head `3cb0ec989ceca296b29f466cd1d6764bdede7e70` into base `c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 49401bfa148e3f2426fa9b9768f73a896dce309c && git checkout 49401bfa148e3f2426fa9b9768f73a896dce309c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58 3cb0ec989ceca296b29f466cd1d6764bdede7e70 && git checkout -B drift-repro c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58 && git merge --no-ff 3cb0ec989ceca296b29f466cd1d6764bdede7e70

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c934631723b7f8d2d447a73d5e7c3428a08cfb58` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inbox listing and decision admission add the slot for a caller only when `hasPlatformAdminStanding` answers yes at that moment, memoized per request context. Nobody is enumerated or notified. The decision records `actor_id` (the person) and `acted_as` (the slot). At node entry the armed body's package (`flowPackageOf` / `armedFlowPackage`) must be a code-source registry row, or with no row a residual owner a code door recorded; otherwise the node fails closed with FORBIDDEN and writes nothing, and the fallback slate is checked the same way. The runtime save door refuses it (`approval-approver-platform-admin-authored`), and `os lint` refuses nothing. Fix round: `isOverrideActor` takes the pending slate from the override admissions (decide, reassign, recall, viewer `can_override`). A slate holding the platform slot closes only the tenant-admin arm. Whole-request, not per-slot, because an override finalizes the node, so on a mixed slate the ordinary slot holder still decides as a slot holder.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, minor changeset.
- Owed: review-c's L1 ACCEPT read, plus a CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record (Clause-② yes face, and `packages/spec/src` non-test: `approval.zod.ts`).
- Pins: `platform-admin-approver-34218.test.ts` 16/16 (org admin refused with no slot and no override; mixed slate; CONTROL: the platform override arm and the system context unchanged). plugin-approvals 1668 tests, lint 9051, spec 27005 at dc6720f3 (spec untouched since). Ablations: standing forced true → 3 red; slot arm without standing → 3 red; node-entry refusal off → 5 red; atSaveDoor forced each way → red; override guard removed → 2 red; decide-site slate dropped → 2 red.
- Stated deviations: three ratified files (approver-address.ts holds the slot predicates because the approver-address-readers guard refused an inline one); local NOT MEASURED check:skill-examples, check:dual-build-cjs-loads and check:i18n (untouched dists), all green in CI.
- Follow-up filed: #34302 (ui: console pending-approvals feed may omit `platform_admin:*`, inferred).
- Dev reports: 6907548416 on #34218, plus the fix-round report in the area.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cffa4a47133a1a4e6f5207050b812744db386d47`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts

Inputs read: card #34218 (body and all 10 comments), PR #34300 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main`, comments 6907533238, 6908962015, 6908985977), and the 71 check-runs on this head (59 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure). Nothing was built or run. The remainder of the diff (the changeset, `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, the generated `content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx`, the new test file) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ApproverType` gains the member `platform_admin`: an accept-set widening on a published enum. Right, and it is what ruling 6904694980 point 1 orders.
- `APPROVER_VALUE_BINDINGS.platform_admin = { source: 'auto' }`, `APPROVER_ORG_SCOPED.platform_admin = false`, and membership in `NON_AUTHORABLE_APPROVER_TYPES` (so it is published in `xEnumDeprecated` and no designer offers it): right. Both `satisfies Record` tables stay exhaustive, and Type Check is green.
- The `.describe()` sentence and the generated reference agree (the enum row, the three approver tables and the `## ApproverType` section all carry the new member and sentence). `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Build Docs` are success on this head, so the generated baselines are taken as current.
- New public surface in `@objectstack/lint`: the rule id `APPROVAL_APPROVER_PLATFORM_ADMIN_AUTHORED`, the type `ValidateApprovalApproversOptions`, and an optional second parameter on `validateApprovalApprovers`. Additive. Right.
- New optional members on the plugin's `ApprovalEngine` interface (`registry.getPackage`, `residualOwnerSource`) and `ActingCaller.platformAdmin`. Additive, and absent reads as refuse / no slot. Right.
- Runtime accept-set, as declared: a typed `platform_admin` approver opens one slot only from a code-source package's armed body. Right as far as the typed approver goes.
- Runtime accept-set, NOT declared: the diff also changes what some already-accepted flows do, outside the typed approver. Wrong: see M1 (stated at rule level).
- Override admission: the tenant-admin arm is withheld when the pending slate holds the slot, at decide, reassign, recall and `viewer.can_override`. All four call sites pass the pending slate; the five read-grant call sites pass none, as the PR says. Right. The type is new, so no answer served today moves on this account.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). The line is present and well formed in the PR body and in the changeset, and it is the right arm: a new enum member, nothing accepted before is refused.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is right under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 (a new accepted value is `added`; the refusals bind only the new member, so nothing is `narrowed`). The kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and the changeset gives `minor` to `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/lint`. `Check Changeset` is success. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed.

The level is right for what the PR declares. M1 means the diff publishes a wider behaviour than the declaration states; the fix closes that, and the level does not move.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6905239693, open question (which `Metadata-protocol` value): answered `added` by claim amendment 6905259267. Closed.
- Dev report 6907548416, open question 1 (withhold the tenant-admin override): answered B. It is on the card only inside claim amendment 2 (6907614406, "per the seat's ruling B"), not as a seat ruling of its own. See N5.
- Dev report 6907548416, open question 2 (three files outside the literal path list): answered A, ratified in claim amendment 2 (6907614406). Closed. All three files are in this record's scope.
- Stated deviation, three checks NOT MEASURED locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`): the check-runs on this head carry no failure, so they are answered there.
- `security_findings: "none"` in both dev reports: not upheld. See M1, M2 and S1.
- Out-of-scope finding (console pending feed may omit the slot): stated as filed as #34302. Not read here, and not a finding against this diff. N3 names a second gap that #34302 does not cover.
- Cloud lane confirmation that its flow ships in a `code`-registered package (ruling 6904772436, last line): not on the card. It does not block this PR; it blocks cloud#4632 using it.

### ④ Design judgment

**Spec schema face (`packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`).** Read against rulings 6904694980 and 6904772436 and against the first consumer, `resolveApproverSpec` and `openNodeRequest` in the approvals runtime.

- The member is added with no `value`, auto binding, not org-scoped and not authorable. This is what the ruling orders, and the runtime reads it the same way: the type returns the one slot before any directory read, and an `organization` on it is refused by the existing directory-less rule.
- The enum comment, the `.describe()` text and the JSDoc on `value` say what the runtime does for a typed approver. The sentence "the approval node refuses to open anywhere else" is true of the typed approver only; M1 is where it stops being true of the slot.
- No must-fix and no should-fix arises in this file by itself. Nits N2 below.

**Clause-② widening face (the implementing files).** Read sentence by sentence against the rulings, and attacked.

What holds:

- Who takes the slot. `resolveActor` admits a caller naming the slot, and `actingCaller` adds it to the default actor, only on the answer of `hasPlatformAdminStanding(engine, userId)`. That is the one per-user predicate, reused and not re-derived, with no organization scope, read from stored rows and never from the envelope's posture. An organization administrator, an ordinary member and a revoked administrator get no slot. An impersonated session is judged as the impersonated user. A system context is exempt as before, and no system caller in this package mints an actor for the slot.
- The memo is keyed by the execution-context object and then by user id, in a `WeakMap`. No cross-user reuse is possible. Cross-request reuse needs a context object that outlives a request; the one transport that reaches these doors builds a context per request, and the shared system context carries no user id and so is never a key. Safe today. See N1.
- Listing. The inbox and the participant probes take the slot from the same `actingAddresses`, and a client-named approver id only narrows what the caller may already see. A caller without standing cannot list by the slot.
- Override. The tenant-admin arm is closed at decide, reassign, recall and `viewer.can_override` when the pending slate holds the slot; the platform arm and the system context are unchanged; on a mixed slate the ordinary slot holder is admitted as a slot holder and recorded with `acted_as` their own address. `sendBack` admits slot holders only.
- Naming the slot as a hand-over target. Reassigning to it and SLA-escalating to it are both refused by the existing target rule.
- Nobody is enumerated or notified. The notification fan-out, the action-link person lookup and the label reader all treat the address as naming no person. No path was found that lists the platform administrators. A decision records its decider (`actor_id`) beside the slot (`acted_as`), as ruled, so the readers of that one request learn that its decider holds platform standing; that is the ruled design, not an enumeration.
- Provenance of a typed approver. The refusal reads `armedFlowPackage` (never `packagedFlowOwner`), then the registry row's `source`, then the residual-owner record, and refuses on any unknown, unreadable or non-`code` answer, before any slate is read or row written. `approvers` and `fallbackApprovers` are both judged. Every running-environment door that registers a package states `authored` or `marketplace`; none states `code`.
- Save door. The runtime publish gate passes `atSaveDoor`, and both `approvers` and `fallbackApprovers` are refused there with `approval-approver-platform-admin-authored`; the CLI commands refuse nothing. This agrees with ruling 6904772436 ("early feedback, not the gate").

What does not hold. Three findings are security-class. They are stated here at rule level only; the mechanism is held back in a separate note for the seat.

M1 (must-fix) — The rule of ruling 6904772436 point 2 is "only the running body of a code-source package's flow may put a request on the platform administrators' slot". On this head that rule is enforced for one way a slate comes to hold the slot and not for every way. A tenant author, and in one form an ordinary user, can open a request on the slot from a flow that is not a code-source package's, and neither the node-entry refusal nor the save door answers it. On `main` the same input opens on the organization's administrators instead, so this is behaviour the diff introduces. It breaks the card's addendum point 2 and the ruling's pin "a tenant flow naming the type is refused" in substance. No pin in `platform-admin-approver-34218.test.ts` covers it.

M2 (must-fix) — The rule of seat ruling Q1 = B is that a step holding the slot is the platform's to decide, and that nobody on the tenant side decides it in the platform's place. On a slate that holds the slot beside an ordinary approver, a caller with no platform standing and no override can change who holds the platform's place on the request, so that the platform's part of the decision can come from inside the tenant. The PR publishes the mixed slate as supported (changeset, guide and pin), so the boundary must hold on it. The first consumer's pure slate is not affected. No pin covers it.

S1 (should-fix) — The origin rule must be answered about the same body whose step is being opened. On this head that is not guaranteed in every run state, so a step can be admitted on an origin that is not its own, and, the other way round, a code package's own step can be refused. The ruling names node entry as the gate and the save door as early feedback only, so the gate has to hold without the save door. I found no tenant door that reaches it today without first passing the save door, which is why this is a should-fix and not a must-fix.

Nits:

N1 (nit) — The standing memo has no time bound; it is correct only while every transport builds a fresh context per request. A sentence saying so on `platformAdminStanding`, or a follow-up card, is enough.

N2 (nit) — In `approval.zod.ts`: the docblock of `NON_AUTHORABLE_APPROVER_TYPES` still says "One source: the deprecated spellings", and the list is published as `xEnumDeprecated`, so a reader of the JSON schema sees `platform_admin` labelled deprecated when it is not. A `value` on a `platform_admin` approver is ignored, not refused (stated in the PR's acceptance notes). Prose fix, or an accepted deviation.

N3 (nit) — The inbox listing keeps the caller's active-organization filter, as the PR states. A platform administrator whose active organization is not the request's can decide the request by id but will not find it in the list. The card's business reason is "it sits in no one's queue", and the request's organization is the publisher's, so the cloud lane should confirm this before cloud#4632 relies on it. Follow-up card; #34302 covers the console identity list only.

N4 (nit) — The PR body's quick-read section says 14 tests where the file has 16. The reassign refusal text calls the slot "a slot literal no approver acts under", which is no longer true of this slot, though the refusal itself is right. The slot's display label is the raw address.

N5 (nit) — Seat ruling Q1 = B is on the card only as a reference inside claim amendment 2 (6907614406). It was relayed to this review thread and is taken as given; the seat should post it on #34218 as a ruling of record.
